_readme: PLAYABLE CONFIG — copy over <server>/UserData/rtsai.json to play AGAINST the
alien AI, then restart the server (or let the current round end; the file is
This is rtsai.example.json with the four soak scaffolds turned off and the
military layer turned on at bring-up step 2 — defence executes, offence does
not. See rtsai.example.json for what every key means; the comments here only
cover what DIFFERS from a soak.
IN GAME: /rtsai mil prints posture, portfolio and every battalion.
_playable: testMode false is the one switch that separates a soak from a game: no
forced round end, no map cycling, no combat suppression, humans are not
bankrupted. suppressCombat only applies while testMode is true, so its
value below is inert and kept only to be explicit.
storageBufferCaches 0 — the free Bio Cache pile is a measurement scaffold
and has no business in a played game.
configCycle off — the A/B rig owns workerCapPerBioCache and producerPerSites
while it cycles, and there is no experiment here to protect.
_military: BRING-UP STEP 2: execute true, offence false.
The AI garrisons its Nest and sends grouped responses to Bio Caches that are
both EARNING and THREATENED. It will not attack you.
Step 1 if you want to watch it think first: set execute false. Nothing moves,
and [DEFENCE] / [MISSION] / [BATTALION] still print the whole portfolio.
Step 3 once defence looks sane: set offence true. The army then pushes when
its own value stops growing while cash is available — expect this to be the
wrong call at first, it is the least measured thing in the mod.
WHAT TO WATCH, in this order:
1. the garrison stays home and does not chase,
2. responses ARRIVE TOGETHER — a trickle means requiredValue is too low,
3. units are not tugged between vanilla and us (visible as stutter),
4. combat.jsonl finally gets rows with "sides":2. Those are the first
real exchange ratios this project has ever had, and they are what
cashPerThreat and strengthMargin should be set from.
TOO PASSIVE? raise cashPerThreat — it prices every defender. TOO EAGER, or
stripping the base to answer a raid? lower it, or raise homeShare.
_lockAlienCommander: The alien commander seat is returned to the AI within a second of anyone
taking it. Not a courtesy: the moment a human commands the aliens the game
disables the AI commander, EcoPlanner stands down and every military tick
declines to order anything — the thing being tested silently stops running
while the round carries on. [ALIEN/LOCK] says so when it fires.
Leave false for co-op, where a human commands aliens on purpose.
_maxNodeFronts: Hard ceiling on how many fronts may be NODING at once, above every budget
the planner computes for itself — the per-tick node fire budget, the escape
hatch, and pioneer chains all obey it.
The planner funds fronts from surplus and will open six or more on a deep
bank, which is what the eco soaks wanted. Two is what a game wants: broad
noding spreads structures no defence can cover.
_eco: Otherwise unchanged from the soak configuration — this is the tuned economy.
